article_title: Frameworks for mass collaboration, adaptable scripts, complex systems theory, and collaborative writing
citation: Ludvigsen, S., Law, N., Rosé, C. P., & Stahl, G. (2017). Frameworks for mass collaboration, adaptable scripts, complex systems theory, and collaborative writing. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn, 12, 127–131. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-017-9257-7
title: A3C framework: attendance, coordination, cooperation, and collaboration as interaction types for designing mass collaboration activities
description: The editorial describes the A3C framework, presented by Jeong, Cress, Moskaliuk, and Kimmerle, which organizes mass collaboration (such as co-editing a Wikipedia page or working in Scratch) into four interaction types: "attendance, coordination, cooperation, and collaboration, which they refer to as the A3C framework". How participants choose to interact depends on "their goals, tasks, artifacts, and more generally, the environment". The framework implies social interaction can range from "rather loose or highly committed and intense".
requirements: Interaction choices must be understood relative to participants' goals, tasks, artifacts, and the environment in which actions are performed
constraints: The four types of interaction should not be viewed as a monotonic progression from simple to advanced, or seen as strongly interdependent
target_learners: participants in online mass collaboration communities and MOOCs
target_learning_goals: learning through mass collaboration and coordinated social interaction
examples: The editorial cites co-editing a Wikipedia page and working in Scratch as design contexts for the framework
key_sources: Ludvigsen, S., Law, N., Rosé, C. P., & Stahl, G. (2017). Frameworks for mass collaboration, adaptable scripts, complex systems theory, and collaborative writing. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn, 12, 127–131. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-017-9257-7

article_title: CSCL: a learning and collaboration science?
citation: Baker, M., Reimann, P. (2024). CSCL: a learning and collaboration science?. International Journal of Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-024-09433-4
title: A3C framework: a broad model of joint participation in large online knowledge communities
description: The editorial cites Jeong et al. (2017)'s "A3C" framework as a broad and useful model for joint interactions in large online knowledge communities. It "integrates different forms of participation, from 'attendance' (being a community member observing the ongoing knowledge building processes), to coordination, cooperation and finally collaboration." The editorial uses it to interpret how mass participation in a MOOC depended on the tools used.
requirements: Applies to large online knowledge communities rather than small synchronous groups
target_learners: members of large online knowledge communities and MOOC participants
target_learning_goals: collaborative knowledge building in mass online settings
examples: Yang (2024) drew on the A3C framework, combined with socio-emotional analysis, to study mass participation in a MOOC on basic maths, finding participation forms differed between a Danmaku environment and discussion board threads.
key_sources: Baker, M., Reimann, P. (2024). CSCL: a learning and collaboration science?. International Journal of Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-024-09433-4
